meta.title: Automatic ECG signal-quality checker
meta.tools: Signal-quality indices (kurtosis, band-power ratio, template agreement) on MIT-BIH + NSTDB noise with known noisy segments
meta.summary: Flag unusable 5-second ECG segments automatically using three signal-quality indices, and measure sensitivity and specificity against segments where real electrode-motion noise was deliberately added at known times.
meta.problem: Wearables record hours of ECG, much of it corrupted by movement. Can software recognise which parts to trust?
meta.theory:
Clean ECG is spiky (kurtosis ≫ 3), has most power in 5–15 Hz relative to 5–40 Hz (QRS band ratio ≈ 0.5–0.8), and consecutive beats look alike. Noise
lowers kurtosis toward 3 (Gaussian) and shifts power outside the QRS band. A segment is flagged if 2 of 3 indices fail; expected detection is
good at ≤ 0 dB SNR and poor at ≥ 12 dB, where the noise barely changes the waveform.
meta.method:
Record 100 (30 min) with NSTDB 'em' noise added in alternating 2-minute blocks at SNR −6, 0, 6, 12 dB; 5-s segments labelled noisy if inside a noise block. Thresholds
chosen on record 101 (same procedure), tested on record 100.
meta.data: Real: MIT-BIH records 100/101 + MIT-BIH Noise Stress Test Database electrode-motion noise (PhysioNet).
